purpose: Dated external open-loop Performance observations, report-ingress budget acceptance and bounded Preview operations closeout; existing Performance and deployment Owners remain authoritative.

window.semantics: Seven calendar dates, not seven guaranteed runs or results; the observation window is not complete.

interpretation: 15,709 known HTTP-accepted submissions lacked a Result in the first observation window; original submissions completed successfully during drain. They were not unknown submissions.
All four campaigns confirmed owned connection cleanup; cleanup Worker state unknown is distinct from an unknown HTTP submission.
These are open-loop case results, not saturation, maximum TPS, every-moment availability or a latency SLA.

reportIngress.counterMeaning: Sampled per-Dispatcher cumulative dropped Reports; not exact total, unique Workers or Task Results.
reportIngress.temporalAssociation: 10k campaign stop waves; warning lacks event type, so individual dropped report classes are not confirmed.
reportIngress.consequence: Lossy scheduling serviceability evidence can retain stale HOT supply; physical route revocation and Task Result queues are independent. DEFAULT does not probe retained HOT coordinates.

fleetSample.scope: 200 bounded sampled stopped Performance Workers, not a fleet-wide census

preChangeRuntimeSnapshot.limits: Point-in-time idle resources and retained maintenance evidence, not server resources collected during the four load runs.

reportIngressBudget.status: configured and observed in an independent published-kit 10k run; original case states retained

sourceRegression.claimLimit: Source regression evidence remains separate from the actual public run.

maintenanceFailure.initialApply: failed: atomic replacement omitted service group and Runtime could not read configuration
maintenanceFailure.interpretation: These five failed starts are a known failure in this maintenance operation; they are independent of the earlier lifecycle events with unknown causes.

restorePointCleanup.scope: only this operation three configuration/metadata files; no Redis/SQLite/user/Worker data

maintenanceInterval.limits: Operation-start to restored-UP confirmation, approximately four minutes twenty seconds; not every-instant availability probes or an exact outage-duration measurement.

persistentWorkers.recoveryKind: manual existing Lab start after Runtime maintenance and the initial configuration-access failure; not automatic reconnect proof

operationalMetadata.meaning: Current-state prose corrected; retrospective occurrence times are separate from recording time. No historical cause or operator was invented.
operationalMetadata.scope: Metadata-only corrections completed before the report budget maintenance; original logs remain authoritative.

postChangePublicAcceptance.status: completed with original workload, report and case states

notPassedAttempts.outcome: failed before any external job; no external workload started

manualCallerCorrection.change: normalize numeric dispatch input before shared consumer invocation

postStopFullSchedulingCensus.claim: complete fixed owned identity set in this read window; not every-moment connectivity or all overload/failure cases

postChangeKernelDropCounterEvidence.meaning: No new matching Runtime Report WARN in the inspected post-maintenance log; full owned-set scheduling census confirmed recovery in this read window. This is not a durable drop counter or every-moment guarantee.

postChangePublicAcceptance.countsNote: planned reflects actual case windows. task-any-2000 stops at 10 seconds for in-flight-cap; notSent is generator-side, not HTTP429. All statuses are copied from existing report; no new pass criterion.

activeLoadServerResourceSnapshot.source: independent on-host point read during this run; not the external runner server sampler
activeLoadServerResourceSnapshot.limits: systemd MemoryCurrent/MemoryPeak are cgroup readings, not process RSS. MemoryPeak is the unit-lifetime high-water mark, not a maximum uniquely attributable to this run. This is not a continuous load-resource trace; shared-page RSS must not be summed as exclusive usage.

interpretation: Runner and GitHub success do not mean all nine cases passed: eight passed and task-any-2000 was saturated by the original in-flight-cap rule.

The saturated case measured 10 seconds instead of the nominal 30-second window. The 40,000 requests outside that shortened window were not attempted; 1,859 of the actual 275,000 planned requests were not sent.
All 273,141 sent submissions received known HTTP responses and all accepted Results succeeded after drain; 6,841 Results were not observed in the first wait window.
No new performance threshold, retry, workload reduction or status reinterpretation was introduced. This is not a 2,000 TPS, maximum-capacity, every-moment connectivity or SLA proof.

nonclaims: The seven-date observation window is not complete; only the four elapsed dates are covered.
The original task-any-2000 saturated outcome and all shortened-window/not-sent counts are preserved; this does not establish sustained 2,000 TPS.
The original 200-Worker pre-change sample is distinct from the later complete 10,000-owned-Worker census.
KERNEL best-effort evidence loss is a real scheduling-evidence gap; no Task Result loss is inferred from that warning.
The full census and inspected warning window do not prove every-moment zero disconnection or immunity to every overload/failure.
Manual persistent Worker recovery is not automatic reconnection proof.
The four scheduled campaigns did not collect Server/Redis/JFR load-time samples; the separate acceptance snapshot is one point read.
The known configuration-access failure during this maintenance does not establish the cause of the earlier Nginx or standing Host lifecycle events.
Neither PR125 nor this public acceptance establishes that the separate Android close/public projection issue is fixed.
No private raw logs, credentials or full Worker/request/Task identities are included.
The maintenance start-to-readiness interval is approximate; it is not a continuously probed outage duration.
